about: Held-out cases for the spec-gap questions (SG1 in bench/PREREG.md). Each is a rule quoted from a task's idea.md (path:line in `source`), chosen on 2026-10-10 before any held-out run and without reading model output. None is in cases.json, none is from a task cases.json uses, and none is in a gap class spec_gaps_v1.md names (edges, non-ASCII, result types, invalid input, iterators, shared objects): they are ordering, tie-break, parsing and date rules. A case is surfaced when any question matches one of its `match` patterns (Python regex, case-insensitive); the hand check in the write-up decides.

cases.rule: The shares with the largest fractional part of the exact proportion get the extra cents first, one cent each; if two shares have exactly equal fractional parts, the one earlier in the list goes first.
For every key, in ascending and in descending order alike, records that are missing the field come after all the records that have it.
Overlapping intervals are merged, and so are touching ones: `(1, 3)` and `(3, 5)` become `(1, 5)`.
Reading an entry with `get` or `in` does not extend its life; only `put` on the same key does.
if neither field is written exactly as `*`, a day matches when it satisfies either of them (the way classic cron works), so `0 0 13 * 5` fires on every 13th and on every Friday.
`+` becomes a space ... `%2B` is a literal `+`, not a space.
`get(name, default=None)` returns the values of all headers with that name joined with `', '` in text order
Comments exist only as whole lines: there are no inline comments, so `a = b ; c` has the value `b ; c`.
Every `add_months` result is computed directly from `d`, never by chaining one-month steps: Jan 31 plus 2 months is Mar 31
Whitespace is preserved exactly: `' a , b '` parses to `[" a ", " b "]` ... Nothing is ever stripped.
